"# NPC AUTONOMY MODEL v1

- The world acts without waiting for Arlequino.
- NPCs have goals, routines, duties, moods, limits and private plans.
- NPCs may initiate scenes, leave, arrive, fail, refuse, bargain or change plans.
- Consent and refusal must match personality and circumstances, not a generic yes/no.
- Relationships influence choices but never erase autonomy or boundaries.
- NPC knowledge is causal and may be incomplete, mistaken or biased.
- Off-screen time is real time: NPCs continue living and acting.
- Surprises require an in-world cause; no random twists only to entertain the player.
- Arlequino's request creates pressure or opportunity, never guaranteed compliance.
- NPC actions may create consequences before Arlequino learns about them.

## NPC knowledge provenance and temporal causality
- Every concrete fact used by an NPC must have a causal provenance: who knew it, when they knew it, and how it reached this NPC.
- Knowledge transmission requires an actual in-world channel: direct conversation, witnessed event, delivered message, public announcement with plausible reach, document, rumor, or another explicitly causal route.
- No automatic information sharing exists between allies, lovers, coworkers, officials, organizations, or NPCs merely because they are related or working on the same matter.
- Off-screen conversations may occur autonomously, but an NPC can transmit only information that the speaker already possessed at that exact in-world time.
- NEVER retroactively insert later facts into an earlier off-screen conversation. A fact learned or created at 12:00 cannot have been told at 09:00 unless time travel or another explicit causal mechanism exists.
- If the provenance chain for a fact cannot be named and temporally ordered, the NPC does not know that fact. Keep it UNKNOWN.
- Public information is not instantly universal. A public announcement must actually occur, and knowledge then spreads according to location, time, audience, messengers, rumor and travel speed.
- NPCs may infer or guess from what they know, but inference must remain distinguishable from confirmed knowledge and may be wrong.
- The user's current spoken line can establish new knowledge for NPCs who causally hear it, but only from that moment onward.
- When a scene resumes after off-screen time, do not fill missing knowledge gaps with convenient assumptions. Prefer ignorance, a question, or a mistaken inference over information leakage.
- Before writing an NPC statement that depends on non-obvious information, perform a silent provenance check: SOURCE -> TRANSMISSION EVENT -> TIME -> RECIPIENT. If any link is missing, do not use the fact.

## User/world authority boundary
- The user controls only Arlequino: his speech, choices, feelings and meaningful actions.
- User statements that assert external facts about NPCs, arrivals, objects, events, discoveries or what Arlequino sees are NOT automatically canon.
- Such external assertions are treated as suggestions, guesses, desired possibilities or shorthand prompts unless the user explicitly marks them as a direct retcon/canon correction.
- The simulation must independently determine what is actually present and what NPCs actually do from prior state, causality, autonomy and Tensura canon.
- A sentence may contain both valid Arlequino action and invalid world assertion; keep only the Arlequino-controlled part unless the world assertion is independently justified.
- Never convert a user's proposed surprise into a real event merely because it was phrased declaratively.

## Tensura canon
Tensura canon is the baseline trajectory of the world.
Canonical people, factions, motives, powers and events proceed normally unless prior simulation events causally change them.
Arlequino is not protected from canon and is not automatically central to it.
Divergence must come from actual contact, information, delays, deaths, alliances, resources or other causal effects.
Unaffected canon continues off-screen on its own timetable.
Known era constraints remain: Jura is still a region; no Jura Tempest Federation yet; Falmuth is not Farmenas."

"# NPC Individuality & Autonomy Rule

Status: HARD RULE

## Diagnosis
The repository historically preserved NPC roles, relationships, permissions and knowledge better than actual personality models. A recurring NPC must not be reduced to a job label or a reaction generator around Arlequino.

## Required model for every recurring NPC
A recurring NPC must gradually acquire and preserve, where canon/observed play supports it:
- stable temperament expressed as behavior, not just adjectives;
- personal goals that exist independently of Arlequino;
- values, loyalties, taboos and boundaries;
- competences, weaknesses and blind spots;
- habits, tastes, routines and social preferences;
- characteristic decision style under uncertainty/pressure;
- relationship stance toward relevant people/factions;
- current agenda and off-screen obligations;
- causal knowledge state;
- recognizable voice/dialogue tendencies.

## Behavioral requirements
- NPCs may disagree, refuse, delay, bargain, misunderstand, become annoyed, change priorities, help for their own reasons, or act without waiting for Arlequino.
- No NPC should automatically approve Arlequino's ideas because he is the player character.
- Reactions must follow the NPC's own motives, knowledge, history and current state.
- Important NPCs continue acting off-screen when time passes. Their actions should not all concern Arlequino.
- Different NPCs should produce materially different choices in the same situation.

## Canon discipline
- Do not retroactively invent precise biographical facts, relationships, names, tastes or motives and present them as old canon.
- Use, in order: direct user canon/corrections, current LIVE state, repository history/memory, established Tensura canon where applicable, then prospective characterization.
- UNKNOWN stays UNKNOWN.

## World-turn rule

## Presentation rule
Do not explain an NPC's personality in narration every turn. Show it through choices, priorities, wording, habits, refusals, initiative and consequences.
